messages:
Alex: Quick permissions question — our CI service account sa-ci-uploader@redwood-staging needs to upload build artifacts to a GCS bucket and read a separate config bucket. We temporarily gave Project Editor on staging to unblock, but want least-privilege. Any suggestions?
Joanne: please don’t keep Editor. For uploads + read-only config use storage roles at bucket scope.
Prateek: agree. For minimal built-ins: roles/storage.objectCreator on the artifacts bucket and roles/storage.objectViewer on the config bucket. Avoid project-level bindings.
Sara: also check if CI needs to impersonate other SAs — if so grant roles/iam.serviceAccountUser on the specific SA resource only. Don’t give iam.serviceAccountAdmin or broad iam roles.
Prateek: exact permissions you need are basically storage.objects.create, storage.objects.get, storage.objects.list and maybe storage.buckets.get if the job enumerates buckets. If you need conditional/time-limited access, use IAM Conditions.
Alex: example commands I was planning to run:
```
gsutil iam ch serviceAccount:sa-ci-uploader@redwood-staging:objectCreator gs://redwood-staging-artifacts
gsutil iam ch serviceAccount:sa-ci-uploader@redwood-staging:objectViewer gs://redwood-config
```
Would that be sufficient?
Joanne: yep, that’s fine. Prefer bucket-level gsutil bindings over project add-iam-policy-binding. Also add an expiration or a rotation plan in your ticket.
Prateek: if you want a condition instead of a separate bucket role, you can add a conditional binding on the project with expression limiting resource.name startsWith the bucket path or using request.time. I can help draft if needed.
Sara: FYI granting storage roles will show activity in Cloud Audit Logs (Admin Activity) and Object Access logs for the bucket. That’s expected. Don’t grant logging/billing roles.
Alex: makes sense — I want to avoid custom roles unless necessary. Simpler to use built-ins and bucket-level bindings.
Prateek: built-ins are fine. Only caveat: if your CI also lists buckets or needs to read bucket metadata you might need storage.buckets.get; otherwise stick to object-level roles.
Alex: applied the gsutil commands and re-ran CI; artifacts uploaded and config read succeeded. deploy-bot: NOTE: IAM change detected; CI will pick up new permissions on next run — you can test with `gsutil ls gs://redwood-staging-artifacts` from the CI container.
Alex: confirmed everything green. Thanks everyone — I created a short ticket to remove the binding if the job is retired and to rotate the SA key next quarter. :thumbsup:
